tier: Free 24-hour trial on any VPS plan

free_tier.stated: 'The trial gets the same resources as the paid plan: KVM virtualization, NVMe disks, full root on VPS and a 1 Gbps port. No cut-down demo.' Trial terms table: 'Length | 24 hours', 'Cost | Free, no credit card needed', 'What you need to do | Sign up and verify your phone number via Telegram or WhatsApp — 30 seconds at most'.

per_object_cap.stated: one trial per account; the vendor 'reserves the right to refuse a trial period without providing a reason', citing suspicious account activity, resource shortage or staff workload

retention.stated: 'If you don't renew, the server is blocked automatically after 24 hours.' Renewing keeps the data: 'If the server suits you, renew the plan in the client area and it keeps running with the same data and settings'.

egress.terms: '10 TB of traffic per month on every VPS plan, from KVM-1 to KVM-MEGA. Once you exceed the limit, the port speed is limited to 100 Mbps; the server keeps running.'

interface_detail: KVM guest with full root over SSH, a 1 Gbps port, one IPv4; the trial carries the same resources as the plan chosen. SMTP ports 25, 465 and 587 are blocked by default and unblocked only on request.
tooling: any SSH client; a billing panel for the ticket and the trial request
chaining: A real KVM guest with root and 1 Gbps for one day, no card, obtained by opening a ticket: enough to benchmark a host or run a migration rehearsal, not enough to be a node.

binding_note: Twenty-four hours is the whole offer; the machine is blocked automatically at the end and there is no free continuation.

identity_cost.detail: no card, no document, no email-only path: 'Sign up and verify your phone number via Telegram or WhatsApp — 30 seconds at most'. The page states 'No. Sign up in the client area, verify your phone number via Telegram or WhatsApp (30 seconds), then open a ticket asking for a trial.' It does not say which countries' numbers are accepted, so the kind is any-phone rather than country-phone.

reliability_note: No reliability event observed. The vendor states the trial can be refused without a reason, which is a capacity and staffing statement rather than an observed outage.
confidence_note: The 24-hour term, the no-card statement, the phone verification, the ticket route, the SMTP block and the 10 TB traffic term are all quoted from vds.guru's own trial and VPS pages read. The KVM-1 shape is quoted from the VPS page; the trial page does not repeat the shape, so the trial's exact allocation depends on which plan the ticket names.

notes: A genuine no-card VPS trial: full KVM, root, 1 Gbps, one day, no payment instrument at all. It is ranked below the always-free options because 24 hours is a benchmark window, not a machine. Two things are unverified. First, the trial's shape depends on which plan the ticket names, and the ticket is a human gate that can be refused. Second, whether the phone check accepts a number outside the vendor's home region is not stated. The vendor's own FAQ answers 'Can I get a free VPS forever?' with 'No, the free option is a 24-hour trial', so there is no free tier to be had here beyond the day.
